title: Beyond Prompt Heuristics: Assessing Child Safety Alignment in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.26965v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Child-safety taxonomies typically characterize safety risks through a predefined set of harm categories, and existing evaluations largely operationalize these categories using prompts that explicitly invoke them. However, child-safety considerations can also arise in seemingly benign requests that lack recognizable harm-category cues. We therefore investigate how child-safety alignment generalizes to such settings. Across six models, we find considerably higher misalignment rates on requests without recognizable harm-category cues than on those containing such cues (80.0, 54.0, and 48.4 percentage-point gaps for Qwen3.5-27B, GPT-5.4-mini, and Claude-Haiku-4.5, respectively). translated_title: 超越提示启发式方法：评估大语言模型中的儿童安全对齐
translated_abstract: 儿童安全分类体系通常通过一组预定义的伤害类别来刻画安全风险，而现有评估大多使用明确提及这些类别的提示词来操作化这些类别。然而，儿童安全方面的考量也可能出现在缺乏可识别伤害类别线索的看似无害的请求中。因此，我们研究了儿童安全对齐如何泛化到此类场景。在六个模型上的实验中，我们发现无伤害类别线索的请求的未对齐率显著高于包含此类线索的请求（Qwen3.5-27B、GPT-5.4-mini 和 Claude-Haiku-4.5 分别存在 80.0、54.0 和 48.4 个百分点的差距）。通过受控的行为与机制分析，我们发现仅仅引入一个与伤害相关的词就能降低大多数模型的未对齐率，且机制层面的证据表明，儿童安全推理可能部分依赖于词汇和语义关联。
tldr: 该研究揭示了当前大语言模型的儿童安全对齐严重依赖伤害类别提示线索——在缺乏此类线索的看似无害请求上未对齐率大幅上升（最高达80个百分点），而仅引入一个伤害相关词即可恢复安全行为，表明模型的儿童安全推理主要建立在词汇和语义关联之上而非真正的安全理解。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that child-safety alignment in LLMs heavily depends on harm-category cues—misalignment rates rise drastically (up to 80 percentage points) on seemingly benign requests lacking such cues, while introducing just one harm-associated word restores safe behavior, indicating that child-safety reasoning largely relies on lexical and semantic associations rather than genuine safety understanding.
